## Verdict

**Acme Desk** costs least for a team of 35, at **$280 per month**. Its $8 per-seat rate is the lowest on the list and its 10-seat minimum sits well below the team size, so all 35 seats bill at list. Fennel HQ is next at $420; Kelp is the most expensive at $850, because its 50-seat minimum forces payment for 15 seats the team will not use.

## Vendors

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Acme Desk | $8 | 10 |
| Fennel HQ | $12 | 25 |
| Kelp | $17 | 50 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 35 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Acme Desk:** minimum 10 < 35, so 35 seats paid. 35 × $8 = **$280 per month**. Effective rate $8.00 per person.
- **Fennel HQ:** minimum 25 < 35, so 35 seats paid. 35 × $12 = **$420 per month**. Effective rate $12.00 per person.
- **Kelp:** minimum 50 > 35, so 50 seats paid. 50 × $17 = **$850 per month**. Effective rate $24.29 per person ($850 ÷ 35); 15 unused seats worth $255.

Acme Desk is $140 per month cheaper than Fennel HQ and $570 per month cheaper than Kelp — $1,680 and $6,840 per year.

## Risks

- **Kelp's penalty is a minimum-seat artefact.** It disappears at 50 people, where Kelp bills $17 per seat against Acme Desk's $400. Acme Desk still leads on list price at every size in this range.
- **Growth and shrinkage.** All three scale linearly above 50 seats, with Acme Desk's absolute lead widening. Below 25 people, Fennel HQ starts billing its 25-seat floor; below 10, Acme Desk bills its own.
- **Price only.** The price list carries no information on features, support tiers, usage limits, security, or integrations, so the cheapest seat may not be a comparable product.
- **Billing terms fixed.** Figures assume monthly billing at list, as stated. Annual commitments, volume discounts, onboarding and migration costs are not on the price list and could reorder these totals.
